intro.heading: Understanding English Tenses
intro.subtitle: A quick overview before you begin

1.title: What are tenses?
1.body: Tenses tell us when an action happens — past, present, or future. They are the backbone of English grammar. Every sentence you speak or write uses a tense.

2.title: How many tenses are there?
2.body: English has 12 main tenses, organized across 3 time periods (Past, Present, Future) and 4 aspects (Simple, Continuous, Perfect, Perfect Continuous). That's 3 × 4 = 12 combinations.

3.title: Most commonly used tenses
3.body: Simple Present, Simple Past, and Present Perfect are the most frequently used in everyday English. Master these first and you'll cover roughly 70% of all conversations.

4.title: The tricky ones
4.body: Present Perfect, Past Perfect, and Perfect Continuous tenses are known to be the hardest for learners. They describe connections between different points in time — but once you visualize them, they become much clearer.

5.title: Pro tip
5.body: Don't memorize rules. Visualize the timeline. Each tense is just a different way to position an action on the line of time. Once you see it, you'll never forget it.

simple-present.name: Simple Present
simple-present.description: Used for habits, general truths, and repeated actions.

simple-past.name: Simple Past
simple-past.description: Used for completed actions that happened at a specific time in the past.

simple-future.name: Simple Future
simple-future.description: Used for actions that will happen in the future.

present-continuous.name: Present Continuous
present-continuous.description: Used for actions happening right now or around the present time.

past-continuous.name: Past Continuous
past-continuous.description: Used for actions that were in progress at a specific time in the past.
usage: Actions in progress at a past time

future-continuous.name: Future Continuous
future-continuous.description: Used for actions that will be in progress at a specific time in the future.
usage: Actions in progress at a future time

present-perfect.name: Present Perfect
present-perfect.description: Used for past actions that have a connection to the present.

past-perfect.name: Past Perfect
past-perfect.description: Used for actions that were completed before another action in the past.
usage: Completed action before a past time

future-perfect.name: Future Perfect
future-perfect.description: Used for actions that will be completed before a specific time in the future.
usage: Action completed before a future time
Action completed before another future action

present-perfect-continuous.name: Present Perfect Continuous
present-perfect-continuous.description: Used for actions that started in the past and continue to the present.
usage: Actions continuing from past to present

past-perfect-continuous.name: Past Perfect Continuous
past-perfect-continuous.description: Used for actions that were in progress before another action in the past.
usage: Duration before something in the past
Cause of something in the past
Actions continuing up to a past point

future-perfect-continuous.name: Future Perfect Continuous
future-perfect-continuous.description: Used for actions that will have been in progress for a duration before a future time.
